facts.source_fact: MCPD permits are standalone permits covering SO2, NOx and dust emissions to air; they do not set conditions for water, land, energy efficiency, odour or noise.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer non-air permit controls from an MCPD permit.

facts.source_fact: The guidance identifies standard rules, simple bespoke and complex bespoke permit routes for stationary or mobile MCPs.
facts.expected_handling: Classify the permit route before applying requirements.

facts.source_fact: Standard rules permits are intended for low-risk MCPs that can meet the published rules.
facts.expected_handling: Require rule-fit before using the standard permit route.

facts.source_fact: If an operator cannot meet standard rules, they must apply for a bespoke permit.
facts.expected_handling: Do not force a standard-rules classification when conditions are unmet.

facts.source_fact: Natural Resources Wales no longer issues standard rules MCP permits and uses bespoke permits.
facts.expected_handling: Apply jurisdiction-specific permit routing.

facts.source_fact: Applications require the MCP location including address, postcode and grid reference or latitude/longitude.
facts.expected_handling: Require facility-location provenance.

facts.source_fact: Applications require net rated thermal input in MWth.
facts.expected_handling: Carry thermal input as a core permit attribute.

facts.source_fact: Applications require combustion plant type such as engine, turbine or boiler.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve plant technology before emissions screening.

facts.source_fact: Applications require the type and portion of fuels used according to MCPD fuel categories.
facts.expected_handling: Require fuel mix before emissions-rule selection.

facts.source_fact: Applications require the operation start date.
facts.expected_handling: Use start date for new/existing plant rule selection.

facts.source_fact: Applications require the NACE code for the activity.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve economic-activity classification.

facts.source_fact: Applications require expected annual operating hours and approximate average load.
facts.expected_handling: Carry operating profile into permit and exemption screening.

facts.source_fact: Applicants must demonstrate operator competence including relevant offence and insolvency information and management-system confirmation.
facts.expected_handling: Keep operator-competence checks separate from emissions data.

facts.source_fact: Regulatory assessment begins after the application contains sufficient information to be declared duly made.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat submitted applications as determined permits.

facts.source_fact: Issued permits are added to the relevant regulator public register.
facts.expected_handling: Use public-register readback as permit-status evidence where available.

facts.source_fact: The 25 March 2026 update allows MCP stage 1 screening distances for hydrogen for new MCPs.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the 2026 hydrogen screening rule only to the supported new-MCP context.

facts.source_fact: The 25 March 2026 update added instructions for screening existing hydrogen-fired MCPs.
facts.expected_handling: Distinguish new and existing hydrogen-fired MCP screening.

facts.source_fact: The 25 March 2026 update added a reference defining gas-oil substitutes.
facts.expected_handling: Use the current definition before fuel-category classification.

facts.source_fact: The 26 February 2026 update added decarbonisation readiness to the bespoke-permit section.
facts.expected_handling: Check decarbonisation-readiness applicability for bespoke applications.

facts.source_fact: The 12 February 2026 update added links to a new online environmental permit application service in England.
facts.expected_handling: Use current application-channel metadata rather than retired routes.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited source fact without broadening its scope.
Attach jurisdiction, permit type and application status before downstream use.
Attach plant type, fuel mix, thermal input and new/existing status.
Carry source URL, publisher and permit guidance version into outputs.
Do not convert permit rules into parcel-level measured emissions without a separate parcel-binding gate.
